threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflows and confirm scope of SOP and QC upgrade.

messages.text: Hi team, let's kick off the 'Standardised Sample Handling and QC Upgrade' project. To start with T1, could everyone briefly share how their shift currently handles sample reception and initial QC? We need to map out the existing process to see where the variations are.

On the morning shift, samples come in, we check the forms, assign a lab number, and then sort them by test type. QC is mostly visual - checking for haemolysis or insufficient volume. It feels like the evening shift does the labelling slightly differently though.

That's right. The evening shift pre-labels tubes which can sometimes cause mix-ups if a collection is cancelled. A major pain point is handling irreplaceable samples like CSF or bone marrow aspirates; there's no standard procedure, it's just based on who is on duty. We need to get this documented.
Sorry, what do you mean by 'pain point'? Is that just anything that goes wrong?
Confirming the morning shift process. Also, our daily equipment QC checks are on paper logs next to the machine, but I've noticed not all columns are filled in consistently across shifts.

@47527 A 'pain point' is a recurring problem or inefficiency in the process. So for example, the lack of a standard procedure for precious samples is a major one because it creates risk and inconsistency.

Thanks all, this is very helpful. I've captured these points in the current state workflow diagram A8. Based on this, I propose for the first version we focus on standard blood (serum, plasma, whole blood) and urine samples. We can tackle complex samples like bone marrow in a later phase. Does that sound reasonable?
Yes, that makes sense. Let's get the high-volume workflows right first.
Okay, I understand. Focusing on the main sample types first is a good idea.
Agree with the scope. It's ambitious enough as it is.
Great. Now for the pilot. We need to pick one shift to test the new procedures before we roll them out everywhere. Any thoughts?
The night shift could be a good candidate. Their sample volume is generally lower, which would give them more time to adapt and provide detailed feedback without being overwhelmed.
That's true, but the night shift also has less senior staff available for support if they run into a complex issue with an analyser or the new SOP.
What about the morning shift? They handle the highest volume and variety. If it works for them, it will work for anyone. It would be a real stress test.

Both are valid points. A stress test is good, but so is ensuring the team feels supported. How about we select the morning shift, but we formally schedule one of us to be 'on-call' for immediate questions during the pilot week?
The on-call support model works for me. That mitigates the risk.
I agree, that's a good compromise.

Okay, so to confirm our decisions:
1. Scope for the first SOP version will be standard blood and urine samples. (D1)
2. The pilot group will be the morning shift, and we will arrange on-call support for them. (D2)
I'll make a note of this.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the unified sample handling SOP draft.

messages.text: Hi all, I've created the 'Draft Unified Sample Handling SOP v0.3' (A1) based on our discussion. I'd appreciate your review on the core steps in sections 2-4, which covers T2. The section on waste handling (T5) is a placeholder for now. @526208, could you take a look at that part specifically?
Of course. I'll review the waste handling section against our current Environmental Guideline A3 and add my comments directly in the document by tomorrow.

I've reviewed the draft A1. Good start. A few critical points: Section 3.2 on centrifugation needs to specify different protocols (g-force/time) for serum vs plasma tubes. Also, for EDTA tubes awaiting analysis, storage must be at 2-8°C, not room temp as stated, to preserve nucleic acid integrity. I've added this as a comment.

This is very detailed. One question on the labelling section for T8. It says to use the 'Patient ID'. Should we use the unique hospital number (UHN) or the specific visit/accession number? Sometimes the forms have both and it's not clear.
@147659 Excellent catches, especially on the storage temperature. That's a crucial detail. I'll update the document immediately.
@47527 That's a great question, clarity is key here. It must always be the unique hospital number (UHN). I will make that explicit in the SOP and add an example.
I've read through it. The PPE section is good, but we should probably specify that any samples from high-risk wards require double-gloving, just to be safe and consistent with biosafety guidelines.

Update: I've added my suggestions to A1 for the waste disposal section (T5). The main point is ensuring segregation of chemical waste (e.g. from analysers) and biohazardous sample waste at the point of generation. I've proposed a colour-coding system for the bins, referencing A3.

Thanks everyone for the thorough feedback. I'm incorporating all these changes. Now, let's finalize the standardized labelling scheme as part of T8. I've outlined three potential formats in Section 4.1 of A1. I'm leaning towards Option B.

Option B is the strongest. It includes a 2D barcode which is essential for future-proofing and reducing manual entry errors. Option A is too basic and Option C has too many fields for high-pressure situations.
I agree, Option B is the easiest to read quickly.
Option B works for me as well.
Yes, Option B is the one.
Excellent, we have a consensus. I'm marking these two key decisions as closed. I'll update A1 to reflect this and share the next version shortly.

Just to be perfectly clear: we are approving the core sample reception, labelling, and storage steps as documented with the changes discussed (D3), and we are choosing labelling Option B with the 2D barcode as the standard (D4).

threads.thread_goal: Lock down QC checklist, competency checks and training approach.

messages.text: Hi team, as per T3 and T6, I've drafted the 'Routine QC and Equipment Maintenance Checklist' (A2) and the 'Technician Competency and Sign-off Checklist' (A6). They are in the project folder. Please review and let me know if they are practical for daily use.

Thanks @58820. Looking at A2, the daily QC for the haematology analyser is missing a check for on-board reagent levels. We had to rerun a whole batch last month because of that. It's a critical pre-run check.
The competency checklist A6 looks solid. For the sign-off process, who should be responsible? Any senior tech, or specifically the shift lead? I'd suggest the shift lead for better accountability.
That's a very good point, I'll add the reagent level check to A2 right away. Thanks.
I was thinking any senior tech for flexibility, but you're right, having the shift lead sign off is better for consistency. I'll update A6 to specify that.
Will we get training materials before we have to do the competency check? It would be helpful to see what's in the training first.

Absolutely. I'm finalizing the training slides and quick reference cards (A4) for T4 and will share a draft by EOD. @58820, let's ensure the competency points in A6 map directly to the key steps in the SOP and A4.
Another one for A2: the monthly maintenance for centrifuges must include a documented rotor inspection for micro-fractures. It's a key safety and audit point.
Noted. I will add rotor inspection to the monthly checklist in A2. Thanks for the detailed review.
With the additions from @147659, are we ready to approve the QC checklist A2 for the pilot?
Yes, looks good to me.
Yes, with those changes it's ready.

Perfect. Decision D5 is made: the QC checklist A2 is approved. @58820 please upload the final version. Now for D6, the competency criteria. We've agreed on shift lead sign-off. Any other feedback on A6?

For the competency 'Identifies and performs corrective action', we should require the trainee to walk through a real or simulated scenario, not just answer a theoretical question. It's a better test of practical skill.
That's a great idea, makes the assessment much more robust. I'll update A6 to include a scenario-based question for that competency.
So to summarize for D6: we agree on the competency criteria in A6, with the addition of a scenario-based assessment for corrective actions, and the sign-off must be done by the shift lead.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot rollout and incident reporting.

messages.text: Team, announcement: The pilot for T7 will begin next Monday. The morning shift will start using the new SOP (A1) and QC checklist (A2). All materials are in the shared folder.
Confirmed. I've briefed the morning shift lead and they've shared the location of the new documents with their team.
The 'Pre-analytical Error and Rejection Tracking Log' (A5) is set up and ready for T9. I've also entered the data from the last four weeks to establish a baseline for comparison.
To ensure we're all aligned, what are the specific success metrics we'll be tracking during the pilot? Is it just rejection rate, or are we also looking at sample processing time?

Good question. For this one-week pilot, let's keep it focused. We will track two key things: 1) The pre-analytical error rate, which we'll log in A5. 2) Qualitative feedback, which includes any issues, questions, or suggestions. All staff on the pilot shift must use the new 'Deviation Report Template' (A7) to log these (for T11).
Can you post a link to where the template A7 is saved? I want to make sure I can find it easily if someone asks me.
Of course, it's in the main project folder. I've also pinned it to the top of this channel for easy access.
So, to formalize the decision: The pilot will run from next Monday to Friday. We will track success via the pre-analytical error rate in A5 and qualitative feedback logged using A7. This confirms D7.
Sounds good. I'll be on the morning shift Tuesday and Wednesday, so I can provide direct support and observe how things are going.
I can be the on-call support person for Thursday and Friday.
Quick update from day 2 of the pilot: Things are going smoothly. We had one deviation logged in A7 - someone noted that the new standard labels don't adhere well to tubes that are already frozen.
Thanks for flagging that @47527. That is excellent, actionable feedback. Let's add it to the list of items to review at the end of the week.
Just checked the error log A5. We've had 3 labelling errors logged so far this week. The baseline average for the same period was 8. It's early, but that's a positive sign.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate results, lessons learned and final rollout adjustments.

messages.text: Hi team, the pilot week is officially over. A big thank you to the morning shift and everyone who supported them. I've analyzed the 'Pre-analytical Error and Rejection Tracking Log' (A5) and the feedback forms. Key result: we saw a 60% reduction in labelling errors. I'll share a full summary shortly.

That's great news. I'm starting to draft the final summary report for T12. The main qualitative feedback points were the issue with labels on frozen tubes and some initial confusion about the new waste bin colour-coding.

We absolutely must solve the frozen tube label problem before a full rollout. We should probably source a different label type with cryogenic adhesive. Also, this is a good time to start T10 and draft the addendum for bone marrow and stem cell samples. The core principles of the new SOP will apply, but we need specific instructions for cryopreservation and chain of custody.
The waste bin confusion is an easy fix. I can create a simple, visual colour chart and add it to the training pack A4. We can also put up posters at the disposal stations.
So what are the exact changes we need to make before we tell everyone to start using the new process?

Let's list the required adjustments before full rollout:
1. Source and validate new labels for frozen samples.
2. @526208 to update A4 with a waste bin colour chart.
3. @147659 to draft the SOP addendum for T10.
Does that cover everything?
Yes, that covers the critical feedback from the pilot.
Agreed. I can have the chart ready by tomorrow.
Excellent. Now, let's set a date for the full, lab-wide rollout. If we can get the new labels ordered this week and train the other shifts, can we aim to go live on the Monday after next?
That timeline seems feasible. It gives us enough time to run the training sessions for the evening and night shifts without rushing.
That works. I can get the draft for the T10 addendum done by Wednesday this week.

Okay, I will record the decision. D8: We will make three final adjustments (new frozen sample labels, waste bin chart in A4, T10 addendum). The full lab rollout is scheduled for the Monday after next. I'll send out a calendar invite for the training sessions.
Perfect summary, thank you @47527. This has been a great team effort. @58820, please make sure the final report for T12 reflects these outcomes. Great work everyone.
